Permission predicate and page directory range walk used by fast lookup
Slow acquisition and longterm pinning protocol including locking and fault handling
Page cache fetch, folio grab, movable migration, unpin and sanity helpers

findings.text: Three fast acquisition wrappers validate caller arguments and delegate to a common fallback. The only variant enforces FOLL_GET plus FOLL_FAST_ONLY with no slow path. The general fast variant enforces FOLL_GET while preserving caller choice. The pin fast variant enforces FOLL_PIN. All return pinned count on success or EINVAL on bad arguments.

Three pinning wrappers target different locking contexts. Remote pinning operates on an explicit memory descriptor and adds FOLL_PIN with FOLL_TOUCH and FOLL_REMOTE, using caller lock state or a local default. Current pinning operates on the caller descriptor with FOLL_PIN. Unlocked pinning operates on the caller descriptor and adds FOLL_PIN with FOLL_TOUCH and FOLL_UNLOCKABLE from unlocked state. All return zero on invalid arguments, otherwise delegate to longterm locked acquisition.

A memfd folio pinning service pins a byte range from a memory file into caller array with bounded count and reports offset inside first folio. A memfd folio allocator supplies missing folios, handling huge and regular files differently. A folio pin adder increases pin count on an already pinned folio after a debug check for dma pinned state.

Huge page reservation services manage future allocation guarantees. One routine reserves a range for an inode with optional area, returning change count or negative errno. A companion releases a range and adjusts block accounting and pool balances. A reserve allocator dequeues a folio when reservation count remains, otherwise returns null.

Fast lookup returns zero when the build lacks support or the range is not permitted. When FOLL_PIN is requested it samples the write protect sequence before the walk and rechecks after; on concurrent modification it releases what was pinned and reports zero, otherwise it sanity checks pinned pages. The fallback rejects disallowed flag combinations, records pinned history, aligns untagged start, detects length overflow and task size breach, returns fast result when complete or fast only, else continues with slow remainder and merges counts, preserving partial pins on slow failure.

Memfd pinning accepts only shared memory and huge page files, rejects negative or inverted ranges, zero maximum, missing file, and end beyond file size. Huge files use huge page shift and order to convert byte offsets to indices. First pinned folio determines reported intra folio offset. Missing cache entries trigger allocation, with already existing treated as retryable. Movable folio check repeats the whole pass on retry signal, and any terminal error releases already grabbed folios.

Reservation is skipped for no reserve areas. Shared and missing area cases use the inode map with change computation, while private areas allocate a fresh map sized to the range and attach ownership. Charging, subpool and global accounting precede region insertion, with race adjustment when concurrent insertion reduces the needed delta and full unwind of pool, cgroup and map on failure. Unreserve tolerates missing map, adjusts inode blocks by freed amount, and returns pool and global balances.

Fast lookup blocks interrupt driven page table reclamation by disabling interrupts around the page directory range walk, explicitly avoiding reader lock alone because it would not block relevant inter processor signals. Pin requests additionally serialize against fork write protection through a sequence counter sampled with try begin and validated with retry check. The fallback declares a read lock dependency on the address space lock when slow path is allowed.

Reserve folio dequeue holds the huge page lock with interrupts disabled while testing and decrementing reserved count. Unreserve updates inode block count under inode lock and balances subpool and global counters. Huge file folio creation serializes cache insertion with a hashed fault mutex held only around the add step, after zeroing and marking up to date outside the critical section.

Sharable huge areas carry a dedicated lock object with reference count and read write semaphore plus back pointer, created once and stored in private data. Release takes the semaphore for writing before detaching and dropping the reference. Reservation maps carry their own reference count, spin lock, region list, read write semaphore, in progress count and region cache, with cgroup uncharge info cleared for shared use and set for private use.
Test context holds a mutex guarding longterm operations, a pointer array for longterm pages, and a count of longterm pages.

Reservation map layout comprises reference management, synchronization primitives, a regions list and a region cache list with cache count, progress tracking, and optional cgroup accounting fields for counter pointer, per huge page factor and subsystem reference. Huge area lock layout comprises reference management, a read write semaphore, and an associated area pointer mirrored in the area private field.

Fallback progresses through validation, fast attempt, completion decision, slow remainder, and merge. Validation rejects bad flags and addresses. Fast attempt runs first. If it satisfies the full request or fast only was asked, its count is final. Otherwise the start and array advance past what fast pinned and slow acquisition handles the rest with FOLL_TOUCH and FOLL_UNLOCKABLE semantics, merging slow count with fast count while preserving fast pins if slow fails.

Pinning iterates until movable handling settles. Each pass recomputes indices from byte range, drains contiguous cached folios by grabbing each with pin semantics until bound or range end, allocates a single missing folio when lookup yields nothing, and releases batch references. After the range is covered it runs a movable migration check; a retry signal repeats the outer pass, otherwise the pinned count or error is returned after restoring allocation context.

Reservation moves from lock preparation through map selection, change sizing, cgroup charge, subpool and global accounting, region commit, and return of change count, with compensating unwind on each failure edge including pool return, cgroup uncharge, region abort, and lock release. Private failure also drops the freshly allocated map and clears ownership. Unreserve moves through optional region deletion, block adjustment, and pool plus global release.

Callable entry points accept a start address, page count, flag word and page pointer array. Fast only and fast variants return integer count or negative invalid. Pin variants return long count with zero for invalid arguments. Remote pinning additionally accepts a target descriptor and optional locked flag pointer. Unlocked pinning starts from unlocked state.

Memfd pinning accepts file, byte start and end, folio array, maximum and offset out parameter, returning pinned count or negative errno. Memfd allocation accepts file and index, returning folio pointer or error pointer. Huge reserve accepts inode, range bounds, optional area and flag set, returning change count or negative errno. Huge unreserve accepts inode, bounds and freed count, returning zero or negative split failure. Reserve folio dequeue accepts state, preferred node, mask and allocation mask, returning folio or null.

Concurrent fork write protection during dma pinning must fail fast rather than expose torn permissions. Interrupt context reclamation of table pages and cross cpu table synchronization require interrupt blocking, not only reader locking. Missing huge area lock degrades sharing and risks stale pages past file size until removal. Region deletion requiring a split can fail when descriptors are exhausted. Test dumping must clamp out of range one based indices to zero before use.

Address handling uses PAGE_SHIFT with PAGE_MASK plus untagged conversion and TASK_SIZE_MAX limit, with huge shift and order plus per page scaling. Flag words use FOLL_WRITE with FOLL_LONGTERM and FOLL_FORCE and FOLL_PIN and FOLL_GET and FOLL_FAST_ONLY and FOLL_NOFAULT and FOLL_PCI_P2PDMA and FOLL_HONOR_NUMA_FAULT plus FOLL_TOUCH with FOLL_UNLOCKABLE and FOLL_REMOTE. Area handling uses no reserve and may share bits with reservation ownership. Status uses EINVAL with EFAULT and EOVERFLOW and ENOMEM and EEXIST and EAGAIN. Test paths use GUP_FAST_BENCHMARK with GUP_BASIC_TEST and PIN_FAST_BENCHMARK with PIN_BASIC_TEST and PIN_LONGTERM_BENCHMARK and DUMP_USER_PAGES_TEST with a dump limit and one based selection.
Debug checks warn when adding pins to a folio not marked dma pinned, and when attaching a reservation map to a non huge or shared area.
